pr_title: Delete conversation if empty after deleting status
pr_body:
This makes sure that when a status is deleted and the conversation it belongs to no longer contains any statuses as a result, the conversation is cleaned up as well. The current situation is that empty conversations are left behind in the database when statuses are deleted.

Fixes #16629
pr_comments: It might be more impactful to only create a conversation record when a status receives a reply, rather than preemptively. This would reduce the conversations table by a ton (I imagine) but it would require advanced refactoring.

> It might be more impactful to only create a conversation record when a status receives a reply, rather than preemptively. This would reduce the conversations table by a ton (I imagine) but it would require advanced refactoring.

Creating only on reply might cause issues when your instance only gets parts of a conversation (e.g. you're following only one of two participants). Imagining toots A, B, C and D, all in the same conversation, and each a reply to the previous one, if your instance gets toots A, C and D, with your proposal, receiving D would trigger the creation of a conversations object, but A would not be attached to it, which might cause issues if it then receives a reply.

EDIT: actually, i guess a `find_or_create_by` could work there, a reply to A would simply find and reuse the conversation object created when D was received. Maybe this doesn't actually matter.

This would still not fix dangling conversations after toot removal, but it would indeed limit the number of conversation objects that will never be actually useful.

@ClearlyClaire Ah, my bad, the field in question was indeed `statuses` rather than `status_ids`. I guess I coincidentally got the expected result through an attribute reader for `status_ids`. As for the proposals above, is there a particular solution that is preferred? I could add an index if that's okay, or I could try your `find_or_create_by` approach, which admittedly does sound a bit trickier to implement from a logic standpoint. If the chain of replies is broken, as in your example, I reckon there wouldn't be a way to retroactively know what conversation a status originally belonged to.

issue_context.title: conversations table is never cleaned
issue_context.body:
### Expected behaviour

When statuses are deleted, empty conversations should not be left behind

### Actual behaviour

I have 7.6 million empty conversations in my database and only 1.5 million conversations with at least one status

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. run an instance for a while
2. check the result of:
    ```sql
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations c
    LEFT JOIN statuses s ON c.id = s.conversation_id
    WHERE s.id IS NULL;
    ```

### Specifications

I am using Mastodon v3.4.1+glitch.
comments: Indeed, there seem to be no code to clean up empty conversations. We might want to add an index to be able to do that efficiently, as there is currently no index on `conversation_id` on `statuses`…

review_comments: This would not work, `Conversation` does not have a `status_ids`, and querying the database to find statuses with the correct conversation would be expensive, as we do not have an index on conversation.
